title: Ep. 71: The Fox and the Hedgehog

sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: We like stories about leaders who have big ideas,
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢讲述那些拥有宏大构想的领导者的故事，

sentences.en: who defy the odds and pursue their goals with messianic purpose.
sentences.zh: 他们不畏艰难，怀揣着救世主般的使命感去追求目标。

sentences.en: Think of Winston Churchill in World War II,
sentences.zh: 想想二战时期的温斯顿·丘吉尔，

sentences.en: or Abraham Lincoln during the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 或是内战时期的亚伯拉罕·林肯。

sentences.en: But what happens when a leader's vision is the wrong one?
sentences.zh: 但如果领导者的愿景本身就是错的，会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: How do we think about people who dream big,
sentences.zh: 我们该如何看待那些怀揣宏大梦想，

sentences.en: At such times, we might prefer a more cautious style,
sentences.zh: 在那种时候，我们或许更倾向于一种谨慎的风格，
倾向于那些稳扎稳打的人。

sentences.en: Those leaders might not score historic triumphs,
sentences.zh: 这些领导者或许无法取得历史性的丰功伟绩，
但他们也很少酿成大祸。

sentences.en: Thousands of years ago, the Greek poet Archilochus summed up this idea.
sentences.zh: 几千年前，希腊诗人阿基洛库斯总结了这个观点。

sentences.en: The fox knows many things, but the hedgehog knows one big thing.
sentences.zh: 狐狸知道许多事，而刺猬只知道一件大事。

sentences.en: That parable has been the subject of much debate over the last 2,500 years,
sentences.zh: 这则寓言在过去2500年里一直是争论的焦点，
即阿基洛库斯到底是什么意思。
这位是心理学家菲尔·泰特洛克。

sentences.en: Various people have offered various interpretations.
sentences.zh: 不同的人给出了不同的解读。

sentences.en: Some people coming out on the side of the hedgehog saying the hedgehog will trump the fox,
sentences.zh: 有些人站在刺猬这一边，认为刺猬会胜过狐狸，

sentences.en: and other people saying no, it really means the fox is going to do better.
sentences.zh: 而另一些人则说不，这其实意味着狐狸会做得更好。

sentences.en: There are different ways to think about the metaphor, but here's how I see it.
sentences.zh: 对于这个隐喻有不同的思考方式，但我是这样看的。

sentences.en: If a fox wants dinner, it has many options.
sentences.zh: 如果一只狐狸想吃晚餐，它有很多选择。

sentences.en: It can chase down a hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 它可以去追捕一只刺猬。

sentences.en: It can find something else to eat.
It can even go without food for a day.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可以一天不吃东西。

sentences.en: But if you're a hedgehog being chased by a fox,
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一只被狐狸追赶的刺猬，
你只有一个压倒一切的念头。

sentences.en: Tetlock thinks this metaphor also describes two cognitive styles in people.
sentences.zh: 泰特洛克认为这个隐喻也描述了人们的两种认知风格。

sentences.en: Foxes have different strategies for different probleMs.
sentences.zh: 狐狸针对不同的问题有不同的策略。
它们乐于处理细微差别。

sentences.en: Hedgehogs focus on the big picture.
They see every problem through the lens of a single organizing principle.
sentences.zh: 它们通过单一的组织原则来看待每一个问题。

sentences.en: The hedgehogs are more parsimonious, more decisive.
In most MBA programs, they'd probably be viewed as better leadership material.
sentences.zh: 在大多数MBA项目中，他们可能会被视为更好的领导苗子。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we have the story of a hedgehog,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将讲述一个刺猬的故事，

sentences.en: a surgeon who changed the world in daring ways.
sentences.zh: 一位以大胆方式改变了世界的外科医生。

sentences.en: His bold style made him a pioneer in what has today become the transgender movement.
sentences.zh: 他大胆的风格使他成为当今跨性别运动的先驱。

sentences.en: It also propelled him to create one of the world's first international medical missions.
sentences.zh: 这也促使他创建了世界上首批国际医疗援助团之一。

sentences.en: Like other hedgehogs, this surgeon experienced outsized success until one day, he didn't.
sentences.zh: 和其他刺猬一样，这位医生取得了巨大的成功，直到有一天，他失败了。
那简直是一场该死的灾难。

sentences.en: Sandy Stone was born in 1936 in the midst of the Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 桑迪·斯通出生于1936年，正值大萧条时期。

sentences.en: Her parents gave her a Hebrew name.
sentences.zh: 她的父母给了她一个希伯来名字。
泽利格·本-纳坦，一个男孩的名字。

sentences.en: That's because her parents thought she was a boy.
sentences.zh: 那是因为她的父母以为她是男孩。

sentences.en: But from a very early age, she knew she was a girl.
sentences.zh: 但从很小的时候起，她就知道自己是个女孩。

sentences.en: This was a long time ago, decades before the modern trans movement.
sentences.zh: 那是很久以前的事了，在现代跨性别运动出现几十年前。

sentences.en: When Sandy was a child, there were no words, no language to describe what she knew about herself.
sentences.zh: 当桑迪还是个孩子时，没有词汇，没有语言来描述她对自己的认知。

sentences.en: It was all of those things.
sentences.zh: 那包含了所有这些感受。

sentences.en: It stayed like that for Sandy all the way into adulthood.
sentences.zh: 这种情况一直伴随着桑迪，直到她成年。

sentences.en: She went to school, became a recording engineer, moved to the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 她上了学，成为了一名录音工程师，搬到了湾区。

sentences.en: All the while, everyone thought she was a man.
sentences.zh: 一直以来，所有人都以为她是男人。

sentences.en: In the San Francisco phone book, she found a promising lead.
sentences.zh: 在旧金山的电话簿里，她发现了一条有希望的线索。

sentences.en: It was a group for gay men.
sentences.zh: 那是一个男同性恋团体。

sentences.en: When she called, they asked if she was gay.
sentences.zh: 当她打电话时，他们问她是不是同性恋。

sentences.en: So they sent her away and told her to try another group.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把她打发走了，让她去试试别的团体。

sentences.en: The outfit they recommended surprised Sandy.
sentences.zh: 他们推荐的那个机构让桑迪感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It was the San Francisco Police Department.
It turned out that the police department was running a counseling unit of sorts,
sentences.zh: 原来警察局当时在运营某种咨询部门，

sentences.en: which they did for the population of transgender people that lived in the San Francisco Tenderloin,
sentences.zh: 这是为了居住在旧金山田德隆区的跨性别群体设立的，

sentences.en: which was sort of the down-and-out skid row section of town
sentences.zh: 那里算是城里破败的贫民窟地带，

sentences.en: that tended to collect people who couldn't afford to live anywhere else
sentences.zh: 往往聚集着那些住不起别处的人，

sentences.en: or who had run out of options.
sentences.zh: 或者已经走投无路的人。

sentences.en: Trans people who ended up in the Tenderloin were at high risk for drug addiction and prostitution.
sentences.zh: 最终流落到田德隆区的跨性别者面临着很高的药物成瘾和卖淫风险。

sentences.en: When Sandy got in touch with the police to ask for help,
sentences.zh: 当桑迪联系警察寻求帮助时，

sentences.en: the first thing they did was to dissuade her from acting on her feelings.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事就是劝阻她不要顺从自己的感受。

sentences.en: And they actually tried to discourage me by taking on a tour
sentences.zh: 他们实际上试图通过带我参观来劝退我，

sentences.en: that reminded me of Dante being led down into the lower circles of hell.
sentences.zh: 那让我想起但丁被引领下入地狱底层的情景。

sentences.en: They really showed me the worst of everything and then said,
sentences.zh: 他们真的向我展示了一切最糟糕的东西，然后说，

sentences.en: are you sure you still want to go ahead with what you're thinking of?
sentences.zh: 你确定还要坚持你现在的想法吗？

sentences.en: And to be perfectly honest, I was not quite sure what I was thinking of.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我当时并不完全确定自己在想什么。

sentences.en: I was just trying to collect information.
And I think it would be safe to say that that's what we were all doing at that time.
sentences.zh: 我想可以肯定地说，那也是我们当时所有人都在做的事情。

sentences.en: Still, the referral to the police turned out to be a stroke of luck.
sentences.zh: 不过，警察的转介最终成了一次幸运的转机。

sentences.en: The cops told her that a center at Stanford University
sentences.zh: 警察告诉她，斯坦福大学的一个中心

sentences.en: had recently started performing what were then called sex change operations.
sentences.zh: 最近开始进行当时所谓的变性手术。

sentences.en: They didn't refer me to Stanford as much as talk about it,
sentences.zh: 与其说是他们把我转介给斯坦福，不如说是谈论它，
把它当作一个伟大的、遥不可及的目标，

sentences.en: the great beautiful shining star in the sky.
sentences.zh: 天空中那颗伟大、美丽、闪耀的星星。

sentences.en: After years of suffering and loneliness and confusion,
sentences.zh: 经历了多年的痛苦、孤独和困惑之后，

sentences.en: the Stanford program felt like a beacon.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福的项目感觉就像一座灯塔。

sentences.en: Sandy felt she might finally have a chance
sentences.zh: 桑迪觉得她终于有机会

sentences.en: to live a more honest, satisfying life.
sentences.zh: 过上一种更诚实、更满足的生活。

sentences.en: But first, she had to convince the gatekeeper
sentences.zh: 但首先，她必须说服那个守门人，

sentences.en: who stood between her and the person she wanted to become.
sentences.zh: 那个挡在她和她想成为的人之间的人。

sentences.en: He ran what was then called the Gender Dysphoria Program at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 他负责当时斯坦福大学所谓的性别焦虑项目。

sentences.en: The gatekeeper of Stanford's Gender Dysphoria Program was a hedgehog.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福性别焦虑项目的守门人是个刺猬。

sentences.en: From a very early age, he had a big-picture idea.
sentences.zh: 从很小的时候起，他就有一个宏大的构想。

sentences.en: He wanted to help a lot of people.
As a small child, when kids in his school were asked to donate money to a charity,
sentences.zh: 小时候，当学校里的孩子被要求为慈善机构捐款时，
他的同学们捐了一角钱。

sentences.en: Don worked in a vegetable garden an entire summer
sentences.zh: 唐整个夏天都在菜园里干活，

sentences.en: Now, I got a letter, a preserved letter that my mother wrote to some of her friends
sentences.zh: 现在，我有一封信，一封我母亲写给朋友的保存完好的信，

sentences.en: saying, Don, he's done something that nobody has ever done.
sentences.zh: 上面写着，唐，他做了一件没人做过的事。

sentences.en: Don's father feared his little boy was consumed with being a do-gooder,
sentences.zh: 唐的父亲担心他的小儿子沉迷于做一个善人，

sentences.en: that he would turn out to be a failure at business.
sentences.zh: 担心他将来在商业上会一事无成。
唐·洛布成为了一名医生。

sentences.en: When he came to Stanford in the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 当他在20世纪60年代来到斯坦福时，

sentences.en: he was a young, ambitious plastic surgeon,
sentences.zh: 他是一位年轻、雄心勃勃的整形外科医生，

sentences.en: very much in awe of his prize-winning colleagues.
sentences.zh: 对他的获奖同事们非常敬畏。

sentences.en: Coming to Stanford, I was overshadowed by the hugeness of what people were doing,
sentences.zh: 来到斯坦福，我被人们所做之事的宏大所掩盖，

sentences.en: So I knew that I had to do something.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道我必须做点什么。

sentences.en: Like maybe, you know, I got to do this somewhere along the line,
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，我得在某个时候做这件事，

sentences.en: because everybody else here is doing it.
sentences.zh: 因为这里的每个人都在做。

sentences.en: Don was looking for a place to make his mark.
sentences.zh: 唐一直在寻找一个能让他有所建树的地方。

sentences.en: One day, a colleague walked out of an examination room and came up to him.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一位同事从检查室走出来，走到他面前。

sentences.en: I said, Don, I want you to see a patient.
sentences.zh: 我说，唐，我想让你看一个病人。

sentences.en: I said, Dave, send that patient away.
sentences.zh: 我说，戴夫，把那个病人打发走。

sentences.en: I'm a Catholic boy from the Midwest, and I'm at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 我是个来自中西部的天主教男孩，我是在斯坦福。

sentences.en: But Don's colleague insisted he meet the patient.
sentences.zh: 但唐的同事坚持让他见见那个病人。

sentences.en: To be clear, this patient was not Sandy Stone.
sentences.zh: 需要说明的是，这个病人不是桑迪·斯通。

sentences.en: And he said, Do me a favor and go in that room.
sentences.zh: 他说，帮我个忙，进那个房间去。

sentences.en: So I went in the room and talked to the patient.
sentences.zh: 于是我进了房间，和病人谈了谈。

sentences.en: And I said, Now, why do you want a sex change?
sentences.zh: 我说，现在，你为什么想要变性？

sentences.en: She said, Well, I was born, and this is what I should be.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，我出生时就是这样，这就是我应该成为的样子。

sentences.en: I said, Well, when did you decide that?
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，你是什么时候决定这样的？

sentences.en: She said, I didn't decide it.
This is what I was born with from day one.
sentences.zh: 这就是我从出生第一天起就有的样子。

sentences.en: No one on the West Coast had received what's come to be known today as gender reassignment surgery or gender confirmation surgery.
sentences.zh: 西海岸还没有人接受过今天所知的性别重置手术或性别确认手术。

sentences.en: In fact, the surgery had been rarely performed across the whole world.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这种手术在全世界范围内都很少进行。

sentences.en: Don was an unlikely choice of doctor.
sentences.zh: 唐是一个不太可能的医生人选。

sentences.en: He was, by his own account, a prim man from the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 据他自己说，他是一个来自中西部的古板男人。

sentences.en: But although Don initially blanched at the idea of gender reassignment surgery, he felt a shiver of excitement.
sentences.zh: 但尽管唐最初对性别重置手术的想法感到退缩，他却感到了一阵兴奋。

sentences.en: He didn't send the patient away.
Instead, he went looking for information.
He consulted with psychiatrists and a few surgeons around the world who'd already performed this kind of surgery.
sentences.zh: 他咨询了世界各地几位已经做过此类手术的精神科医生和外科医生。

sentences.en: What prompted you, this sort of Catholic doctor from the Midwest, to basically take this on?
sentences.zh: 是什么促使你，这位来自中西部的天主教医生，去着手做这件事的？

sentences.en: It seems like an unlikely fit.
sentences.zh: 这看起来不太像是个合适的选择。

sentences.en: It was a wonderful opportunity to do a big thing and to help a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这是一个做大事并帮助许多人的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: Altruism and ambition were always tightly woven in Don's identity.
sentences.zh: 利他主义和雄心壮志在唐的身份认同中总是紧密交织在一起。

sentences.en: He wasn't interested in superficial cosmetic work.
sentences.zh: 他对肤浅的美容手术不感兴趣。

sentences.en: He wanted to change the world.
He decided to take the leap.
In November 1968, Don Law performed California's first gender reassignment surgery.
sentences.zh: 1968年11月，唐·劳布实施了加州首例性别重置手术。

sentences.en: That we were more than prepared for all the things that might happen.
sentences.zh: 我们对可能发生的一切都做好了充分的准备。

sentences.en: It took about three and a half hours.
sentences.zh: 手术大约花了三个半小时。

sentences.en: We did it with the skin graft method.
sentences.zh: 我们采用了皮肤移植的方法。

sentences.en: Don soon became one of the world's leading experts on gender reassignment surgery.
sentences.zh: 唐很快成为全球性别重置手术领域的顶尖专家之一。

sentences.en: A reputation for being a good surgeon and a tough gatekeeper.
sentences.zh: 他以优秀的外科医生和严苛的把关人而闻名。

sentences.en: He turned away many people because he felt they weren't good candidates for surgery.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了许多人，因为他认为他们不适合做手术。

sentences.en: Sandy Stone vividly remembers her first appointment with him in the mid-70s.
sentences.zh: 桑迪·斯通对70年代中期与他的第一次会面记忆犹新。

sentences.en: I go in and sit down and Don is behind his desk and he's wearing his white coat.
sentences.zh: 我走进去坐下，唐坐在办公桌后，穿着白大褂。

sentences.en: And he's very distinguished looking and calm and very friendly and open.
sentences.zh: 他看起来非常儒雅、冷静，而且非常友好、开明。

sentences.en: And he says, well, what can I do for you?
sentences.zh: 他问，好吧，我能为你做些什么？

sentences.en: And I say the first thing that comes into my head, which is, I think I'm a woman.
sentences.zh: 我脱口而出第一句话：我想我是一个女人。

sentences.en: Now, the scene we have is Don behind his desk and me.
sentences.zh: 当时的情景是唐坐在桌后，而我坐在对面。

sentences.en: I have a long black beard and wild black hair.
sentences.zh: 我留着长长的黑胡子，头发凌乱。

sentences.en: I'm wearing a blue shirt, jeans, and engineer's boots.
sentences.zh: 我穿着蓝色衬衫、牛仔裤和工程师靴。

sentences.en: I do not exactly look like I'm thinking of myself as a stereotypical woman.
sentences.zh: 我看起来并不像是一个认为自己是传统女性的人。

sentences.en: And Don looks at me and says, really?
And I say, what should I do?
I mean, I'm totally, I'm completely open to anything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我完全、彻底地接受任何建议。

sentences.en: I really don't know what I should do, what direction I should move in, what's right, what's wrong.
sentences.zh: 我真的不知道该怎么做，该往哪个方向走，什么是对的，什么是错的。

sentences.en: And I'm looking to Donald to tell me.
sentences.zh: 我在指望唐纳德告诉我。

sentences.en: And in my memory of the thing, Donald then says, well, the first thing you should do is lose the beard.
sentences.zh: 在我的记忆中，唐纳德当时说，好吧，你首先要做的是把胡子刮掉。

sentences.en: That was the beginning of Sandy's long transformative journey.
sentences.zh: 那是桑迪漫长蜕变之旅的开始。

sentences.en: Don wanted Sandy to be sure she was making the right decision.
sentences.zh: 唐希望桑迪能确定她做出了正确的决定。

sentences.en: So before he would even consider surgery, Sandy says he told her she would have to live openly and fully as a woman for one full year.
sentences.zh: 所以在他考虑手术之前，桑迪说他要求她必须以女性身份公开、完整地生活整整一年。

sentences.en: It was a requirement based on the reality of the time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个基于当时现实情况的要求。

sentences.en: No one, not Sandy, nor Don, knew what might come from these surgeries in the long term.
sentences.zh: 没有人，无论是桑迪还是唐，知道这些手术从长远来看会带来什么。

sentences.en: It was all a bit of an experiment, a shot in the dark.
sentences.zh: 这一切都有点像实验，是一次盲目的尝试。
对每个人来说都充满了艰辛。

sentences.en: And it was fraught because at that time it was not clear what would happen later.
sentences.zh: 之所以艰辛，是因为在当时，没人清楚以后会发生什么。

sentences.en: We didn't have very many examples of transgender people who had had surgery who went on to have fulfilling lives and lived to tell about it, which is to say,
sentences.zh: 我们没有太多跨性别者在手术后过上充实生活并现身说法的例子，也就是说，

sentences.en: came back later and reported back to the program.
sentences.zh: 后来回到项目组进行反馈的例子很少。

sentences.en: They were experimenting on the fringe of what both medicine and society thought was acceptable.
sentences.zh: 他们是在医学界和当时社会认为可接受的边缘进行实验。

sentences.en: Don was taking risks with his professional reputation.
sentences.zh: 唐在拿自己的职业声誉冒险。

sentences.en: Sandy was taking risks with her life.
sentences.zh: 桑迪在拿自己的生命冒险。

sentences.en: There was one moment, Sandy says, when she and Don clashed.
sentences.zh: 桑迪说，有一次她和唐发生了冲突。

sentences.en: The conflict boiled down to their cognitive styles.
